headline: Thanksgiving's storm brings strong to damaging winds and heavy rain to New York City, peaking late this afternoon into evening, along with widespread moderate coastal flooding at both of today's high tides, with tonight's tide likely the higher one.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: A storm tracking north from the south, squeezed against unusually strong high pressure over the Northeast, brings strong to damaging east-northeast winds and rain to New York City on Thanksgiving. Winds build to about 25 to 30 mph with gusts of 35 to 40 mph this morning, then 30 to 40 mph with gusts of roughly 45 to 58 mph this afternoon, strongest in the city and along the coast, with the peak most likely late afternoon into evening (timing could be off by a few hours); a High Wind Warning covers the city, Long Island and the Hudson County/Newark-area New Jersey waterfront until 1 AM Friday, and a Wind Advisory covers areas farther north and west plus Connecticut until 5 AM Friday. Isolated gusts of 58 mph or more are possible along coastal Connecticut, southern Westchester and eastern Bergen County. The heaviest rain falls late afternoon into evening with a rumble of thunder possible, mostly causing minor street and poor-drainage flooding, though a slight chance of flash flooding remains in the city; rain and wind ease late tonight.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Friday brings a chance of light rain or showers, mainly north and west of the city, with the storm still nearby, and southwest winds gusting about 30 to 35 mph that turn west after midnight. High pressure slowly builds in for a dry Saturday, with west winds gusting about 25 to 30 mph that ease Saturday night. The discussion gives no temperature details for these days.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Sunday stays dry, then showers are likely after midnight Sunday night as a front approaches. A chance of showers lingers Monday morning, with southwest gusts around 25 to 30 mph turning west in the afternoon and northwest Monday night. The discussion gives no detail beyond Monday.

coast: Gale- to storm-force east-northeast winds this morning into tonight, on top of already-high tides after the recent full moon, make widespread moderate coastal flooding likely at both of today's high tides, with locally major flooding possible mainly in southern Nassau and southwest Suffolk along the western Great South Bay, and significant impacts around Peconic Bay and the Peconic River and along the western Long Island Sound shoreline; surge up the Hackensack, Hudson and Passaic rivers brings minor to moderate flooding. The surge now lines up better with this evening's high tide, which will likely be the higher of the two, especially along Long Island Sound, and heavy rain at that time could worsen coastal street flooding; forecasters leaned toward the higher-end water levels for a safety margin. Coastal Flood Warnings run until 6 AM Friday, followed by Coastal Flood Advisories for Friday's morning-to-midday high tide, when winds turn southwest and impacts should be minor to locally moderate; a Coastal Flood Watch remains for parts of Long Island's south shore, though confidence in moderate flooding there has dropped. Ocean beaches see 8 to 12 foot breakers with widespread beach flooding, dune erosion and possible localized overwashes flooding roads and structures behind the dunes, while western Long Island Sound and the Twin Forks see 3 to 6 foot waves with dune erosion, splashover and possible isolated damage to shoreline and marina structures. On the water, a Storm Warning runs until 1 AM Friday, with ocean seas near 20 feet late this afternoon and evening and waves near 10 feet on the Sound and at the New York Harbor entrance; a southwest gale is likely on the ocean Friday, easing to small-craft-advisory levels Saturday and likely below that Sunday, with small-craft conditions possible again Monday, especially on the ocean.
watch_for: Peak winds late this afternoon and evening, whose timing could still be off by a few hours
This evening's high tide, now expected to be the higher one, arriving with the heaviest rain
Friday morning's high tide on Long Island's south shore, still under a Coastal Flood Watch
confidence: Forecasters are confident the strongest winds come late this afternoon into evening even though models still disagree somewhat on exact timing, the coastal flood forecast deliberately leans toward the higher end, and confidence in moderate flooding at Friday morning's tide has dropped.
